budgetTarget: $4,000-$6,500, with slight stretch for exceptional units
scope: Sawtelle / West Los Angeles 3-bedroom candidates from the mapped report, prioritized for whole-unit listings and review/reputation evidence.
methodology: Filtered out obvious co-living/private-room listings for primary rankings.
Prioritized listings near $4k-$6.5k, 3BR/2+ bath layouts, direct listing links, review-source depth, amenity strength, and management/reputation risk.
Used existing mapped listing data plus fresh text-rendered scrapes from VeryApt, Birdeye, ApartmentHomeLiving, Zumper/HotPads/Rent.com where accessible.
sourceLimitations: Rental availability and concessions change quickly; verify every price and unit before applying.
Zillow/Yelp/Apartments.com/ApartmentRatings and some portals may block automated access, so blocked pages are listed as manual-review leads rather than summarized as facts.
Manager-wide reviews do not prove conditions at a specific building, but recurring themes are useful tour questions.
summary: The Adler and 1771 Beloit are the strongest reviewed picks. Maxwell and Stoner1247 look attractive on budget/amenities but need more resident review verification. Wiseman-managed options are abundant and often well-located, but management/package/security/noise questions should be asked before applying.

tourChecklist: Confirm whole-unit rent, not per-bedroom pricing.
Ask for a full monthly fee sheet: parking, trash, utilities, internet, pets, amenities, application/admin fees.
Verify exact unit bath count and floor plan, especially listings with conflicting portal text.
Ask about package theft, garage/car break-ins, bike storage, and controlled access.
Ask about recent maintenance response times, water shutoffs, elevator reliability, noise, and construction.
Tour during evening/commute hours near Santa Monica Blvd, Olympic, Wilshire, Sepulveda, Barrington, Federal, and the 405.
